Proposed effect: Raises discovery, implementation, and maintenance effort
Forum evidence: Matched Temp-control, VENUS 6, Tecan, Cellario, and LiCONiC cases
Alternative explanation: Complex interfaces generate both lower IAS and more support discussion.
Prospective observation: Integration time, failed first commands, escalation count, maintainer dependency
Falsification criterion: IAS has no relationship to implementation burden after controlling for interface complexity.
Study-safe wording: Documentation and support burden covary with interface accessibility in matched cases; causal direction is unresolved.

Proposed effect: Expands the scheduler's executable and observable action space
Forum evidence: Scheduler and driver discussions; phi/lift association
Alternative explanation: Scheduler-focused sampling includes device breadth by design.
Prospective observation: Benchmark completion with controlled driver coverage and simulator access
Falsification criterion: Changing interface coverage does not affect executable-task coverage or failed dispatches.
Study-safe wording: Interface accessibility appears to be an enabling condition for orchestration, separate from scheduling quality.

Proposed effect: Increases divergence between intended configuration and active system state
Forum evidence: Tecan Git/runtime workspace; VENUS state and recovery requests
Alternative explanation: High-complexity systems create both entanglement and recovery problems.
Prospective observation: Configuration-related incident rate, first-divergence location, recovery completeness
Falsification criterion: Fully bound manifests do not reduce configuration ambiguity or recovery uncertainty.
Study-safe wording: Configuration and runtime entanglement plausibly increases recovery and diagnosis burden.
